weather_line: Fog in the hollows · hats accounted for · ducks unaccounted for

stories.headline: Guild Archivist Speaks; Provides Initials, a Region, and a Phrase She Will Not Repeat Twice
stories.byline: By Pemwick, Junior Analyst, Duck Provenance Office — filed Sunday, 8:43 a.m.
body: The Guild archivist, one Mabel Forsythe-Crue, who has reportedly not confirmed anything to anyone in eleven years of service, confirmed something this morning. After forty minutes of considered silence and one cup of tea she did not offer to share, she produced a single handwritten index card from the inner pocket of her cardigan and placed it on the table between herself and this correspondent.

The card read: 'D.H. — Appalachian circuit — leaves them where they'll find them.' She then removed it, replaced it in her cardigan, and said, with great finality, 'That's the phrase.' When asked what phrase, she said, 'The one I won't repeat.' She then wished this correspondent a good morning.

Pemwick, who has been working without a lunch break since Thursday, has confirmed that 'D.H.' does not appear in any current Guild registry, any active Jeep community membership roll, or any Ministry file. The initials do, however, appear in a footnote in the same 1987 appendix — listed, without explanation, as a 'Benefactor, Circuit Unknown.' The Duck Bandit has a name. Or the beginning of one. The investigation is elevated to Priority Amber with a side notation of 'Getting Warmer.'

stories.headline: Ellie Holds Extended Conversation With the Kitchen Window; Window Declines to Reciprocate; Ellie Considers This Progress
body: Sources within the household confirm that Ellie, the golden familiar of indeterminate focus, spent approximately forty minutes on Sunday morning engaged in what she appeared to regard as a meaningful dialogue with the kitchen window. The window, which faces east and has no enchantments of record, offered no response.
Ellie has reportedly interpreted this as patience on the window's part and has vowed to return tomorrow. She left on good terms. The window was unavailable for comment, being a window.

stories.headline: Sunday's Accounts Rest Undisturbed; Goblins Describe Weekend as 'Structurally Sound'; Christine Described Weekend Similarly
body: In a rare alignment of institutional and personal assessment, both Gringotts Senior Operations and Christine have independently characterised this Sunday as 'structurally sound.' The goblins meant the vault ledgers. Christine meant the day. The outcome is the same: no fires, no disputes, no emergency correspondence, all figures correct to the galleon.
Deputy Senior Clerk Harruck, when informed of the alignment, requested it be noted in the weekly summary. It has been noted. The weekly summary is quietly pleased with itself.

stories.headline: Quoyne Reads Sunday Paper; Confirms 'Wholesome, Not Misc.' Registry Shelf 'Still Level'; Considers This Worth Noting
body: Bertrand Quoyne, Senior Filing Administrator and custodian of the 'Wholesome, Not Misc.' registry, paused his Sunday reading this morning to verify, using a small personal spirit level he carries in his breast pocket, that the registry shelf remains precisely plumb. It does. He has made a note of this. The note has been filed.

The registry continues to hold two entries and room for a third. Quoyne declined to speculate on when a third nomination might arrive, but was observed glancing at the empty divider tab with an expression colleagues describe as 'quiet readiness.' The shelf is level. The registry endures.

familiars_corner: Lucy: Has spent Sunday moving between four different observation posts in the household, cataloguing the position of every treat-adjacent surface. She has made no move. She is, colleagues note, playing a very long game.
Ellie: Returned to the kitchen window after lunch, sat down in front of it with great solemnity, and waited. She is not sure what she is waiting for. She is confident it will be wonderful.

Jersey: Found the warmest patch of Sunday light available, arranged himself in it with architectural precision, and has been there since half-past nine. He is unavailable. He is, however, very comfortable, and the warmth is mutual.
founding_editor_note: That archivist's got the right idea — one card, said what needed saying, put it away. No wasted words. I built a whole garage once with fewer instructions than Pemwick's been writing. — D.

in_brief.sport: Sunday Quidditch postponed due to fog; Chaser Briggs described the conditions as 'like flying through a wardrobe full of wool'; no injuries, several damp scarves.
in_brief.forecast: Fog persisting through the gorge until midmorning, clearing to pale autumn gold by noon; a second clearing expected at dusk, described by the Gorge itself as 'atmospheric'; ducks will be where they will be.

storyline_updates.title: The Duck Bandit Returns
storyline_updates.summary: Day 4: The Guild archivist, Mabel Forsythe-Crue, has provided a single index card: 'D.H. — Appalachian circuit — leaves them where they'll find them.' She has declined to elaborate. Pemwick has traced 'D.H.' to a footnote in the 1987 appendix listing them as 'Benefactor, Circuit Unknown.' The Bandit has initials and a territory. Day 5 (resolution): The final edition should reveal D.H. fully — a warmly elusive figure, perhaps a longtime traveller of the Appalachian circuit who leaves hatted ducks specifically for people who take care of their trails and their Jeeps, drawn to Christine and Steve by reputation. The resolution should feel earned and affectionate: the Bandit is revealed not as a prankster but as a recogniser of good people, and the ducks are understood as a kind of blessing from someone who knows the ridgelines. Pemwick files his final report. The Jeep may receive one more duck.
